content.value_statement: Generative art requests often need repeatable code, polished controls, and a clear creative concept. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to create seeded p5.js artwork with reusable viewer controls.
actual_capabilities: Drafts a concise algorithmic philosophy before implementation.
Guides p5.js sketches with seeded randomness and deterministic output.
Uses a viewer template with seed navigation and parameter controls.
Supports sliders, color pickers, reset actions, and PNG download workflows.
Encourages original algorithms instead of copying existing artists.
limitations: Generated HTML depends on external p5.js unless assets are vendored.
It does not include automated browser tests or performance benchmarks.
Artwork quality still depends on the model and prompt specificity.
The template targets browser canvas workflows, not print production files.

use_cases.title: Prototype gallery visuals
use_cases.description: Create a seeded browser artwork with adjustable parameters for a campaign, event, or installation concept.

use_cases.title: Explore creative coding ideas
use_cases.description: Turn a visual theme into a p5.js sketch with reproducible seeds and interactive controls.

use_cases.title: Teach generative systems
use_cases.description: Demonstrate how particles, fields, randomness, and parameters shape an interactive visual system.

prompt_templates.title: Start from a theme
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a complete artwork concept.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an original algorithmic art piece about tidal memory. Include the philosophy and one interactive p5.js HTML artifact.

prompt_templates.title: Control the interaction
prompt_templates.scenario: User wants specific controls and repeatable output.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a seeded generative art viewer with controls for density, turbulence, palette, and motion speed. Keep seed navigation working.

prompt_templates.title: Refine an existing concept
prompt_templates.scenario: User has a draft aesthetic direction.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use my concept of quiet electrical weather. Make the algorithm feel subtle, layered, and deterministic across seeds.

prompt_templates.title: Create a variation system
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced user needs a family of related outputs.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an Art Blocks style system with seed presets, parameter ranges, and a clear explanation of how variations emerge.

output_examples.input: Create generative art inspired by wind over stone.
output_examples.output: A short movement philosophy, followed by an interactive viewer with seeded particle erosion and adjustable field strength.

output_examples.input: Make a calm abstract piece with reproducible variations.
output_examples.output: A browser artwork using deterministic seeds, soft palette controls, reset actions, and navigation between nearby variations.

output_examples.input: Help me explore flow fields for an installation mockup.
output_examples.output: A p5.js concept with tunable density, turbulence, line weight, and seed presets for review.

best_practices: Start with the algorithmic philosophy, then map each idea to a behavior or parameter.
Use seeded randomness for every visual choice that should be reproducible.
Keep the fixed viewer controls intact while changing only the artwork-specific sections.
anti_patterns: Do not copy a living artist or request a direct style imitation.
Do not replace the template with unrelated layout or broken controls.
Do not rely on random colors or particles without a clear generative rule.

faq.question: Does this skill create finished artwork?
faq.answer: It creates a complete interactive HTML artwork concept, including philosophy, p5.js logic, and controls.

faq.question: Can users reproduce the same image?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill emphasizes seeds so the same parameters and seed produce the same result.

faq.question: Does it need a server?
faq.answer: No. The intended output is a single browser artifact that opens directly.

faq.question: Why does it use p5.js?
faq.answer: p5.js is well suited for browser canvas sketches, seeded drawing systems, and interactive controls.

faq.question: Can it make many variations?
faq.answer: Yes. Seed navigation lets users explore related outputs from the same algorithm.

faq.question: Is it safe for commercial style requests?
faq.answer: It instructs models to create original algorithms and avoid copying existing artists.
